tests.summary: 174 of 174 backend (dotnet test) + 40 of 40 frontend (vitest) passing, plus 6 of 6 real-backend/real-browser Playwright tests (e2e/auth-real-backend.spec.ts against a real running API and real migrated database, no mocking). Independently re-verified by the R05 reviewer: same counts (220 total), all passing. Reviewer found both corrected concurrency tests rely on uncontrolled scheduling and can pass through a benign ordering without ever exercising the critical branch (stale-success rejection, or recovery-code rollback) they claim to prove - see blockingIssues.

blockingIssues: ALV-001-C01-R05-01 (P1, evidence gap): the step-up race test starts two uncontrolled concurrent tasks and accepts either outcome, with no barrier/fault hook controlling whether the fifth failure locks before or after the step-up's conditional reset, and no assertion proves both branches actually ran - repeated uncontrolled runs can all take the same benign step-up-first path without ever exercising the stale-success rejection.

ALV-001-C01-R05-02 (P1, evidence gap): the recovery-code rollback tests can pass without executing the rollback branch - the deterministic reproduction marks the code used BEFORE calling CompleteMfaChallengeAsync, so the service's own UsedAtUtc==null query excludes it and the method never reaches the conditional update at all; the two-context race test has no coordination forcing both requests to load/verify the same unused code before either consumes it, so the losing side can likewise bypass the branch entirely and still show a compatible final state.
